prompt: My M5StickS3 already sends wrist-spin speed (rev/s) over BLE to my browser fishing game while the player reels in. Now I want a mini-game where the fish pulls left/right and the player has to spin clockwise to push right and counter-clockwise to push left. Problem: players hold the stick in all kinds of ways. How do I get spin direction on the stick and make it reliable in the game? Give me the firmware part and the JS part.
assertions: The firmware computes spin direction as a sensor axis plus sign (e.g. from integrated gyro rotation and/or cross products of consecutive samples) and sends it in the BLE packet
The firmware handles both twisting around the device's own axis and circular wrist motion where the gyro vector rotates
The firmware reports when the direction is unknown/ambiguous (e.g. a confidence flag or threshold) rather than always guessing
The game learns which axis+sign means clockwise for this device and grip through a calibration step where the player spins in a known direction
The calibration result is stored per device (e.g. localStorage keyed by device name) so it is not repeated every session
The JS maps incoming direction to +1/-1/0 and the mini-game uses it to push the marker right/left
The solution includes keyboard keys for spinning clockwise and counter-clockwise so the mini-game can be tested without the stick
